selected.title: His Therapist Thought His Ex Was His Girlfriend
selected.hook: A couples therapist emailed me homework for sessions I'd never attended.
selected.voiceover:
A couples therapist emailed me homework for sessions I'd never attended.

The message started, ‘After yesterday's session, try the trust exercise we discussed.’ It used my boyfriend's name, but the woman listed beside him wasn't me. It was his ex, Lauren.

We've been together two years. They supposedly stopped speaking before our first anniversary.

I called him and asked one question: ‘Who is Dr. Patel?’

Silence. Then he said Lauren was struggling after a breakup, and he'd joined two therapy sessions to help her get closure.

Except the email included a shared worksheet.

Their answers were about jealousy, communication, future plans, even arguments we'd had in our apartment. He'd been describing my relationship problems in therapy, but presenting Lauren as the partner.

When I confronted him, he insisted nothing romantic happened. He said talking to Lauren was easier because she already understood him.

Then I noticed the appointment history.

Not two sessions. Nine. Every Thursday for three months.

And last week's goal said: ‘Decide whether rebuilding the relationship is realistic.’

He claimed the therapist misunderstood what ‘relationship’ meant.

So I asked why he never corrected her.

He couldn't answer.

I packed a bag and stayed with my sister. Now he's begging me not to throw away two years over ‘therapy that got complicated.’

But if your partner secretly spent three months repairing a relationship with their ex, would you care whether they ever kissed?
selected.youtube_description:
An unexpected couples-therapy email reveals that her boyfriend has been attending sessions with his ex for months. He says he was only helping her get closure, but the therapist's notes describe jealousy, future plans, and relationship problems that belong to his current girlfriend. This relationship drama turns emotional boundaries and secret therapy into one question: does it matter if nothing physical happened?
